topic.angle: Fermi's paper scraps and the logic of rough estimates

body.question: During the Trinity test blast, Enrico Fermi dropped scraps of paper and estimated the explosion's strength from how far they travelled. What yield did he estimate?
body.reveal: About 10 kilotons of TNT, well within an order of magnitude of the now-accepted 21 kilotons. Estimates like this work because over- and underestimates tend to cancel out.

probes.question: Why do Fermi estimates built from several rough factors often land close?
options: Overestimates and underestimates tend to cancel
